title: Dispelling the illusions of liver detoxification | Dr. Naresh Shanmugam
content:
Liver detoxification has become a popular topic in recent times, with many products and diets claiming to cleanse and rejuvenate the liver. However, it’s important to understand that the concept of detoxifying the liver after consuming alcohol is misleading and that there is no scientific evidence behind the same.

Watch this video as Dr. Naresh Shanmugam, Director-Women and Child Health & Senior Consultant-Paediatric Gastroenterology & Hepatology, debunks the myths around detoxification of liver and alcohol consumption.

title: How does alcohol damage the liver | Dr. Naresh Shanmugam
content:
The liver is a vital organ responsible for several crucial functions in the body, including filtering toxins and waste products from the blood, producing bile for digestion, storing essential nutrients, metabolizing drugs and medications, and synthesizing proteins and clotting factors. However, when the liver itself becomes damaged, it can lead to a range of health problems and alcoholism can be one of the primary factors leading to liver damage.

Watch this video as Dr. Naresh Shanmugam, Director-Women and Child Health & Senior Consultant-Paediatric Gastroenterology & Hepatology talks about the harmful effects of alcohol on liver and the stages of liver damage due to alcoholism.

title: Silent Migraine | Dr. Shankar Balakrishnan
department: Department of Neurology, Neurosciences, Rela Centre For Mobility & Movement
content:
Did you know that migraines can be present without a headache?

Silent migraines are referred to a type of migraine where individuals experience typical migraine symptoms but without headache.

A few symptoms of this type of migraine includes visual disturbances, sensory disturbances and cognitive difficulties. It’s important to note that silent migraines can still significantly impact a person’s daily life and overall well-being, even without the presence of a headache.

Watch this video as Dr. Shankar Balakrishnan, Clinical Lead, Neurology, Neuroscience, Rela Centre For Mobility & Movement, talks about this condition in detail.

title: Robotic Surgery Eases Knee Pain
content: 64-year-old Vasumathy had been struggling with knee problem for the past decade. Her condition worsened during the past 6 months. Fortunately she found herself at Rela Hospital where she met with Dr. Ashok S. Gavaskar, Clinical Lead – Orthopaedics, Head – Joint Replacement Services. The doctor and his team thoroughly evaluated Mrs Vasumathy Ramanujum and suggested her with conventional total knee replacement for her left knee. Her test results post surgery showed signs of damage in her right knee as well. She then underwent Robotic right knee replacement at Rela Hospital under the same team led by Dr. Ashok S. Gavaskar. Mrs Vasumathy Ramanujum says her right knee felt more natural and felt less pain post the robotic knee replacement surgery. Her husband, Mr. Ramanujum expressed his gratitude towards the entire hospital and the team of doctors for their unwavering support throughout the process, which facilitated his wife’s speedy recovery. This story highlights the significance of seeking appropriate medical attention and expertise. It also emphasizes the importance of compassionate and dedicated doctors striving to provide their patients with the best care.

Fortunately, he found himself at Rela Hospital, where his daughter spoke to Dr. V. Narendra Kumar (Senior Consultant in Interventional Cardiology, Advanced Heart Failure, and Transplant Cardiology). After undergoing the procedure, Mr. Abdul Rehman was discharged on the third day and had been doing well ever since. He expressed his gratitude towards the entire hospital and the doctor’s team for their unwavering support throughout the process, which facilitated his speedy recovery.

title: Baby Siwansh’s succesful liver transplant | Dr. Jagadeesh Menon VR
content:
Geeta Awasthi’s son, Siwansh Awasthi, from Nepal was undergoing liver problems from when he was one and a half years old. His stomach was bloated and filled with fluid and his skin was pale. He was taken to a government hospital in Nepal where they couldn’t diagnose the exact condition. They were then suggested to be taken to Rela Hospital, Chennai.

The child was thoroughly examined by Dr. Jagadeesh Menon VR, Consultant, Paediatric Hepatology. Upon examining his symptoms and taking a few tests, the doctor confirmed that it was a liver failure and a liver transplantation was the only survival option.

From the sixth day of their visit, the kid underwent liver transplantation by the expert team of doctors and was also discharged within two weeks from the surgery without further complications.

Baby Siwansh is now three years old and is in a much healthier condition as his development and liver function looks normal. The mother was happy to see her child walk and run normally like other children. She expressed her gratitude to all the doctors and staff at the hospital. We wish the child, a good and healthy life in the future.

title: Corn piece removed from patient’s lung in timely procedure | Dr. Benhur Joel Shadrach
content:
Mr. Thanuj’s father, a 55-year-old gentleman, was brought to Rela hospital when a corn kernel got stuck in his lungs.

Upon his arrival, he underwent a CT scan which revealed the presence of a foreign body. On Bronchoscopy examination, a piece of corn of approximately 3 cm in size in the right lung (Right lower lobe basal segment) was confirmed.

An expert team led by Dr. Benhur Joel Shadrach (Consultant- Interventional Pulmonology, Critical care & Sleep Medicine) carried out a bronchoscopic removal of a foreign body using a zero-tip retrieval basket.

After surgery, his lungs improved, and he recovered and was sent home the same day with no further issues. We wish him the best of health

title: Sarshini’s journey with Primary Hyperoxaluria | Dr. Gomathy Narasimhan
content:
Ten months ago, a little girl named Sarshini had been experiencing constant vomiting for a week. Her parents took her to a nearby hospital, where they advised them that it might be a gastric-related disorder. She continued to throw up even after that.

Sarshini was taken to a different hospital where they usually go for consultations, and she was diagnosed with kidney failure. Her creatinine level was above 18 when she underwent dialysis that same day.

A couple of other doctors suggested Rela Hospital to them. She was thoroughly evaluated by Dr. Gomathy Narasimhan (Senior Consultant Liver and Renal Transplant Surgeon HPB Surgery and Liver Transplantation and Renal Transplantation). She was given a genetic test, which revealed that she had the unique condition “Primary Hyperoxaluria.”

She underwent liver and kidney transplants after receiving dialysis for nine months. Sarshini’s grandmother was a liver donor, and her mother was a kidney donor.

Sarshini’s tenacity and bravery enabled her to recover more quickly after the transplant. Both donors and Sarshini are now in good health.

We wish the young girl, also known as a warrior, a good and healthy life in the future.

title: Timely treatment saved this 57 year old’s life | Patient Testimonial
content:
Mr. Sridhar, a resident of Madambakkam, suffered a massive heart attack and was rushed to the nearby hospital for first aid. Later, he was given a choice of moving for further treatment to Rela hospital.

Mr. Sridhar landed at the Rela hospital with a massive heart attack complicated by an issue called complete heart block wherein the heart rate goes below 40 and stays around 40. Due to other complications, he fitted into the high-risk category, and along with that, he had significant viral infections in the blood.

Within an hour of his arrival at the emergency room, he was immediately put into the emergency angioplasty and had the angioplasty corrected. Mrs. Sridhar emphasised the care, comfort and treatment offered by Dr. A. Ashok Kumar (Senior Consultant – Interventional Cardiologist) and his team.

Such positive testimonials are a testament to our treatment and care. We send him our best wishes for health and happiness.

title: A Dramatic Memory loss & Surgery less Breakthrough
content:
An 11-year-old Betsy was brought to Rela Hospital, unconscious, after meeting with an accident on January 2nd while riding a bike and was affected with memory loss. After stabilising her, Dr. Anbuselvam (Senior Consultant Neurosurgery) ordered a CT scan which revealed bleeding throughout the brain, which was not operable. Betsy could not walk, write, or even talk, for that matter.

The prime aim of the doctor was to give a conducive atmosphere for the damaged brain to recover well, keeping all the parameters in a normal range. The doctor calmed down the family, who had been panicking for the past 4 days stating that she was recovering well and did not require any operation. In her condition, with the home environment setup and other rehabilitative care, her right-sided weakness recovered completely.

She began performing her tasks post-operation and gradually started recalling everything. The family is grateful to all the doctors for assisting their daughter in regaining her composure and living a regular, happy life.

title: All About EBUS Procedure
content:
Dr. Benhur Joel Shadrach (Consultant – Interventional Pulmonology, Critical Care & Sleep Medicine Pulmonology Medicine) explains the working of an EBUS. EBUS is a minimally invasive procedure that is used to diagnose lung disorders.

A Fuji EBUS scope comprises an outer scope and an ultrasound processor. With the help of the ultrasound processor, we can sample the nodes on the screen directly. A needle is passed through the working channel for the biopsy. With the help of this, we take a sample of a lesion from the patient which is then shared with the pathologist, who provides an on-table diagnosis.

title: Standing Upright From Scoliosis | Scoliosis Treatment
content:
Mahima, a 12-year-old girl with a severely neglected spine deformity was brought to Rela by her parents after an acquaintance referred us . Owing to potential complications that could arise during a Spine correction surgery, her parents were unable to get a doctor to operate on her at their home country in Sri Lanka. Here at Rela, Dr. Parthasarathy Srinivasan(Senior Consultant – Orthopaedics, Head-Spine Surgery) attended to Mahima. There were few challenges that lay ahead for the team and Mahima during the surgery. Primarily, she had only 2.5 Litres of blood which meant that any blood loss more than 500 ML could prove problematic. Adding to that, she was suffering from a condition that bent her spine to a whopping 140 degrees (Neurofibromatosis). Furthermore, she also had soft bones. The combination of these 3 factors made this a tricky surgery.

However, we went through the surgery successfully. Post operation, she was taken care by the experts at our paediatric ICU for 24 to 48 hours. Currently, she has recovered and is walking, taller and happier. We are ecstatic we could put a smile on the family’s face.

title: A Sudani soldier beats Hip Joint
content:
Mr. Keru Rainey Rainey, the father of Elizabeth Rainey, faced problems with his leg that was shot during a war. He was experiencing relentless pain in his left hip joint. The 6’8″ gentleman used to wear a 7cm high raised shoe which almost weighed as much as a brick wall. This made it all the more difficult for him to get his routine activities done with ease. He wanted to put an end to this.

One of Elizabeth’s friends in India, Mairo, referred us. Here, Dr. Dr Ashok S Gavaskar (Clinical lead, Orthopaedics, Head – Joint Replacement Services, Arthroplasty (Joint Replacement Surgery), Orthopaedics.) recommended that they had to go for a left hip replacement. But there were a couple of complications that lay ahead of them. There was a hip joint migration to the left side, and in addition to this, there was an old gunshot injury in his left thigh that resulted in his shortness of height.

The task was to relieve him from the pain he was facing on a daily basis and regain as much height as possible. Dr. Ashok informed that there was only a 50% chance of him regaining his height before they went ahead with the surgery. The surgery was successful. They brought his hip back to its location and corrected more than 50% of his shortness.

6 weeks later, he was a happy man with a pain-free hip, being able to walk independently after a decade.

title: A Mother’s Prayer Answered!
content:
Chandramathi, a 12-year-old child was suffering from a complex structural condition called Scoliosis caused by Neurofabromatosis, a congenital problem that worsens the spine’s curvature.

Chandramathi’s mother, a hardworking single mother was unaware of Chandramathi’s condition until recently when she went to a hospital in Ambur to get her daughter an X-Ray. The doctor suggested a surgery considering the complexity of the condition and the repercussions it could lead to. Not letting anxiety get the better of them, the mother and daughter duo met with Dr. Parthasarathy Srinivasan (Senior Consultant – Orthopaedics, Head – Spine Surgery) who recommended Rela Hospital for the complex surgery that would enhance Chandramathi’s quality of life and restore hope for the mother. To her surprise and respite, humanity came to their aid and crowd funded the surgery. After the completion of the surgery 3 months back, today, Chandramathi is looking at the horizon with a new lease of life and renewed vigour.
